articles.title: Jeremy Thomas obituary
articles.summary: Film producer who enjoyed his greatest success with the 1987 epic The Last Emperor for which he won an Oscar. Asked whether he had ever cautioned restraint from a director, the film producer Jeremy Thomas replied: “My nature would be to go further and see what we can get away with.” Thomas, who has…
body: Thomas, who has died aged 77, was an expert in getting away with it. A taste for irreverence ran in his family: he was the son of Ralph Thomas, director of the Doctor … comedies that began in 1954 with Doctor in the House, and the nephew of Gerald Thomas, who made all 31 Carry On titles. Jeremy’s own films, however, were risky rather than risque.

Bad Timing (1980), the first of three collaborations with the director Nicolas Roeg, explored a destructive love affair blighted by jealousy, attempted suicide and rape. Rank, the studio behind it, withheld from the start of the print its familiar company ident showing a man striking a gong. According to Thomas, the studio also denounced the picture as “a sick film made by sick people for sick people”.

He teamed up on several occasions with David Cronenberg, first for an adaptation of William S Burroughs’s Naked Lunch (1991), featuring a sentient, fleshy typewriter that talks through its anus, and most infamously for a film of Crash (1996), JG Ballard’s novel about a group of outsiders who get their sexual kicks from car accidents.
points: Film producer who enjoyed his greatest success with the 1987 epic The Last Emperor for which he won an Oscar.
Asked whether he had ever cautioned restraint from a director, the film producer Jeremy Thomas replied: “My nature would be to go further and see what we can get away with.

articles.title: In an age of superhero fatigue, Marvel’s best shot is to think small – and outside the box
articles.summary: Sebastian Stan says he pitched Marvel a mid-budget thriller starring his Winter Soldier character. Perhaps the studio should give it – and other modestly scaled vehicles – the green light. Blink a little and you might think we are back in 2019.
body: And yet it doesn’t really feel like it, largely because it is something of a turnaround for Marvel, after a pretty disappointing 2025 in which all three of the studio’s releases underperformed. Captain America: Brave New World took $415m worldwide, Thunderbolts* managed $382m and even the well-reviewed The Fantastic Four: First Steps stalled at $521m, against a reported $200m budget. These are hardly Madame Web numbers but they do suggest there is still a problem about what to do with all those superheroes who cannot sustain a $300m multiversal extravaganza.

Enter Sebastian Stan, AKA Marvel’s Winter Soldier, who this week suggested the solution might be to place them in cheaper genre films instead. Speaking to New York Magazine, the actor revealed that he had pitched Marvel boss Kevin Feige a new, “Sicario-esque”” approach for Bucky Barnes’ next adventure. “We keep a real small budget,” he said. “It’s about a guy who thinks he recog­nises someone from his past that had something to do with when, you know, he was brain­washed, and he gets obsessed with this per­son. He goes on a whole jour­ney to try to fig­ure out who this per­son is. It’s a thriller.”

Blink a little and you might think we are back in 2019.

articles.title: Ziwe on YouTube as the ‘Great Equalizer’ and Her Only Interview That Went South
articles.summary: Ziwe Fumudoh has built her career in comedy and as an interview host who can handle any guest, from political figures to drag queens. The podcast star and creator screened two episodes from the upcoming season of her podcast “You’d Be an Iconic Guest” — one with comedian and actress Wanda Sykes and…
body: “I think of YouTube as this sort of great equalizer,” she said, noting how hard it is to sell, develop and produce a TV series “YouTube is one-to-one. You create it, and then it’s online. That is the best experience as someone who is artistic, as someone who wants to create art. I do believe that digital creators are the new Hollywood.”

Ziwe’s trademark interview style is both confrontational and comedic. When asked how she balances that style, she said, “I’m a good active listener. I don’t feel the need to fill dead air, and so that is comedic because someone sitting in silence as you sort of ramble is inherently hilarious.”

She also talked about the only interview that ever went south, with the guest ending the conversation after three questions. “Sometimes the universe has different plans for us,” she said when asked why the interview ended.

“It’s an energy thing,” she said. “I think of this as scene work, and these are my scene partners, and so we’re really catching a vibe together. And so I go into it comedy-first. Obviously, the questions and the journalism are part of the entree, but the amuse-bouche is that we are laughing and enjoying ourselves.”

articles.title: Barrio Triste review – raw and dynamic portrait of anarchic slum life in 1980s Medellín
articles.summary: Bad Bunny collaborator Stillz’s debut feature shot using Betacam focuses on vibes over plot. Best known as the creative mind behind the music videos of Puerto Rican rapper and singer Bad Bunny, Stillz has risen to the top of the industry as an in-demand director and photographer.
body: There are moments of crisis here and there – the restless band of youths attempt a robbery and even kill a hostage – yet the primary focus seems to be on vibes rather than plot. The ever-roving camera not only channels the agitated psyche of the main characters but also drums up the chaotic pace of Medellín’s underbelly. One particularly memorable sequence moves from the peculiar sight of a punk duo practising on a rooftop to the garbage-strewn streets, during which seemingly benign interactions can quickly escalate into heated altercations. Echoing the handheld cinematography, life in the slums is unmoored and precarious, as if the ground might give way at any second.

articles.title: ‘The Nature of Invisible Things’ Director Rafaela Camelo Lines Up Luciana Paes and Sundance-Winner Camila Márdila For ‘The Favorite Daughter’ (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.summary: Luciana Paes (“Friendly Beast”) and Camila Márdila (“I’m Still Here”) have been cast in “The Favorite Daughter” (“A Filha Favorita”), the new film by rising Brazilian director Rafaela Camelo.
body: From there onwards, the family drama turns into a road movie through the backlands of Ceará as the two women are forced to confront their own history and rebuild the bond between them.

“The Favorite Daughter” is co-written by Camelo and André Araújo (“Gugu’s World”). The project is a co-production between Brazil’s rising Deberton Filmes via Allan Deberton and Marcelo Pinheiro – whose “Gugu’s World” premiered in Berlin earlier this year and is also gunning for the chance to represent Brazil at the Oscars– and Germany, with Maritza Grass and Vincent Edusei producing for Carousel Film.

Paes is a renowned actress who has appeared in major Brazilian works of TV and film, including Juliana Rojas’s “Necropolis Symphony” and Anna Muylaert’s “Don’t Call Me Son.” Márdila won the World Cinema Dramatic Special Jury Award for Acting at Sundance for her breakout performance in Muylaert’s “The Second Mother,” and went on to feature in other standout films, including Carolina Markowicz’s “Charcoal” and Walter Salles’s Oscar-winning “I’m Still Here.” She has recently wrapped production on Markowicz’s “The Funeral,” one of Brazil’s standout titles for 2027.

articles.title: Heartfelt, Rare Animated Belgian Feature ‘Juul’ Headlines Studio 100 Film’s Expanding Slate at TIFF Market
articles.summary: How far would you go to keep a love one close? Belgian studio Fabrique Fantastique’s debut animated feature “Juul” comes to TIFF Market a few days after Studio 100 Film announced having picked up this young adult animated drama, marking a significant expansion in the otherwise family-driven…
body: “From the first time I read the script, I knew we had something very special in our hands,” recalls Tom Van Gestel, CEO of Fabrique Fantastique, who also leads “Juul” as both director and producer. “If I’m being honest, it was the first I experienced so many emotions and goosebumps while reading a story. And I’ve read (and written) my share. ‘Juul’ drew me in, and I knew we had to be on top of it from the start.”

The script of this rare young adult animated Belgian feature was brought to Van Gestel by An de Gruyter, refined over and over with the studio’s teams. During that process, Fabrique Fantastique alum Liesbet van Loon was also brought on board as art director on the project, to craft this stop-motion like 3D-animated feature. “This technique was a clear choice for us, because of the physicality it brings to our story. ‘Juul’ is all about flesh, and how does one turn from flesh to porcelain, visually speaking.”

articles.title: The Route to Cappyness review – capybara boosterism is an ode to the internet’s favourite rodent
articles.summary: From a cappy-cafe owner in Japan to an escaped capybara in the UK, this homespun film takes the temperature of an international obsession. One of Midlands-based film-maker Sharon Walia’s previous works was The Keepers of the Pigs, proudly described on her production company’s website as “the first…
body: Walia’s celebration of the species stays on script, rejoicing in the animals’ natural geniality, friendliness to other species in their natural habitat, and their compelling, remunerative charm that seems to have bolstered the fortunes of several animal attractions around the world.

Other interlocutors include a cappy-cafe owner in Japan who’s found a great way to get out of the rat race doing what he loves and makes no claims to expertise on the creatures. By contrast, American cappy shillers love to reel off factoids and anecdotes and all sound like they’ve had media training should a camera crew or schoolbus full of kids pull up to the gates. The British cappy-keepers are endearingly more amateur, yet noticeably a little defensive, especially the owners of the park from where Cinnamon, a young female capybara, escaped and made the news and, once again, social media.

articles.title: Oasis confirm Knebworth return and Manchester and Glasgow live 2027 gigs
articles.summary: The band have announced a second wave of shows for their hit reunion tour, after weeks of teasers.
body: After weeks of posting teasers on social media and underneath the Manchester sky, Oasis have confirmed a second leg of their smash hit reunion tour for summer 2027.
The band will return to the scene of their legendary 1996 gigs at Knebworth House to play four nights at the 125,000-capacity venue in September next year.
They will also play a 11-night residency at the home of their beloved Manchester City in June, after kicking off the tour with five gigs at Glasgow's Celtic Park in May.

The announcement dropped on Monday afternoon alongside a new trailer, external and a photograph of frontmen Liam and Noel Gallagher. "Start the celebrations!", read a message on the band's social media.

articles.title: This is what women in sport look like - female athletes hit back
articles.summary: British sprinter Amy Hunt is among an array of female athletes criticising the controversial betting advert starring actress Sydney Sweeney.
body: The advert has gone viral online and features American Sweeney naked but covering parts of her body with various pieces of sporting equipment.

It has sparked a strong reaction, with many female athletes criticising its sexualisation of women in sport, and how they are being defined by their appearance rather than their achievements as sportswomen.

Amy Hunt, who became a four-time European champion earlier this summer, referenced the advert after she ran a season's best 22.10 seconds to finish fourth in the 200m final at the Ultimate Championship in Budapest on Sunday.
"Sydney Sweeney, this is what women in sport look like," Hunt said in her post-race interview with BBC Sport.

body: There’s an energy zipping around New York City these days. Everyone can feel it. And here’s a great thing about it: that energy’s zipping around real-life and fake-life New Yorkers alike.

Right before the Dillard downfall, and right in the midst of his very bad decisions, there’s an episode where Negan finds time to fantasize about a world where he and Maggie met under better, less gruesome circumstances, in New York of all places.
